Well IDs that know their plate

Source: R/well-type.R
well.Rd

A wellr_well vector holds well IDs such as "A01", along with the size of the plate they come from. It is a character vector underneath, so it prints, compares, joins and works with string functions exactly as well IDs always have. Because it knows the plate size, functions such as well_to_index() don't need to be told it.

  • well() creates well IDs, formatting them as "A01".

  • as_well() converts a vector to well IDs, keeping their formatting.

  • is_well() tests whether an object is a vector of well IDs.

  • well_plate_size() and well_plate_dims() give the size of the plate, as the number of wells or as the number of rows and columns.

Combining well IDs from plates of the same size gives well IDs; combining them with plain character vectors, or with well IDs from a plate of a different size, gives a character vector. Use as.character() to get the plain character vector.

Usage

well(x = character(), plate = 96)

as_well(x, plate = NULL)

is_well(x)

well_plate_size(x)

well_plate_dims(x)

Arguments

x

For well() and as_well(), a character vector of well IDs. For the other functions, an object to test or a vector of well IDs.

plate

The plate the wells come from: either the number of wells in a standard plate (6, 12, 24, 48, 96 or 384), or the number of rows and columns. If NULL, as_well() keeps the plate of a wellr_well and otherwise uses the smallest standard plate that contains all the wells.

Value

well() and as_well() return a wellr_well vector. is_well() returns a single logical. well_plate_size() returns the number of wells and well_plate_dims() the number of rows and columns.

Examples

x <- well(c("a1", "B2", "h12"), plate = 96)
x
#> <well<96>[3]>
#> [1] A01 B02 H12

x == "B02"
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
well_to_index(x)
#> [1]  1 14 96
well_plate_size(x)
#> [1] 96

as_well(c("A01", "P24"))
#> <well<384>[2]>
#> [1] A01 P24
